findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance or state file.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, meaning data at rest on the volume is unencrypted and could be exposed if the underlying storage or snapshots are accessed improperly.
The EBS snapshot inherits from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption specified, so snapshot data at rest is unencrypted and could be shared/copied without protection.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from any host on the internet.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no additional restrictions, increasing the attack surface for the web application.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (all ports, all protocols) to 0.0.0.0/0, which can facilitate data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to direct internet access.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to direct internet access.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, potentially exposing sensitive network flow log data.
